:::{#def-matrix-induced-inner-product}
#### Matrix-induced inner product ($\matr{A}$-inner product)

Let $\matr{A}$ be a $p \times p$ [symmetric positive definite matrix](#def-positive-definite).
The **matrix-induced inner product** (or **$\matr{A}$-inner product**)
on $\reals^p$ is defined for all $\vx, \vy \in \reals^p$ by

$$
\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{A}} \eqdef \tp{\vx} \matr{A} \vy.
$$

The space $\reals^p$ equipped with $\iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\matr{A}}$
is an [inner product space](#def-inner-product).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-matrix-induced-inner-product}
#### Properties of the matrix-induced inner product

For every $p \times p$ symmetric positive definite matrix $\matr{A}$,
the function $\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{A}} = \tp{\vx} \matr{A} \vy$ satisfies the four inner product axioms (@def-inner-product):

- **positivity**: $\iprod{\vx}{\vx}_{\matr{A}} = \tp{\vx}\matr{A}\vx \ge 0$ for all $\vx \in \reals^p$;
- **definiteness**: $\iprod{\vx}{\vx}_{\matr{A}} = 0$ if and only if $\vx = \vzero_{p \times 1}$,
  by definition of a positive definite matrix (@def-positive-definite);
- **linearity in the first slot**: for all $\vx, \vy, \vecf{z} \in \reals^p$ and real numbers $a, b$,
  $$
  \ba
  \iprod{a\,\vx + b\,\vy}{\vecf{z}}_{\matr{A}}
  &= \tp{(a\,\vx + b\,\vy)}\,\matr{A}\vecf{z}
  && \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\matr{A}} \text{)}
  \\
  &= (a\,\tp{\vx} + b\,\tp{\vy})\,\matr{A}\vecf{z}
  && \text{(@thm-transpose-sum)}
  \\
  &= a\,\tp{\vx}\matr{A}\vecf{z} + b\,\tp{\vy}\matr{A}\vecf{z}
  && \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib)}
  \\
  &= a\,\iprod{\vx}{\vecf{z}}_{\matr{A}} + b\,\iprod{\vy}{\vecf{z}}_{\matr{A}}
  && \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\matr{A}} \text{)}
  \ea
  $$
- **symmetry**: because $\tp{\vy}\matr{A}\vx$ is a $1 \times 1$ scalar (equal to its own transpose) and $\matr{A}$ is symmetric ($\tp{\matr{A}} = \matr{A}$),
  $$
  \ba
  \iprod{\vy}{\vx}_{\matr{A}}
  &= \tp{\vy}\matr{A}\vx
  && \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\matr{A}} \text{)}
  \\
  &= \tp{\paren{\tp{\vy}\matr{A}\vx}}
  && \text{(a scalar equals its transpose)}
  \\
  &= \tp{\vx}\tp{\matr{A}}\vy
  && \text{(@thm-transpose-product)}
  \\
  &= \tp{\vx}\matr{A}\vy
  && \text{($\matr{A}$ is symmetric)}
  \\
  &= \iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{A}}
  && \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\matr{A}} \text{)}
  \ea
  $$

Conversely, every inner product on $\reals^p$ has this form for a unique symmetric positive definite matrix $\matr{A}$, whose $(i, j)$ entry is $A_{ij} = \iprod{\ve_i}{\ve_j}$, where $\ve_1, \ldots, \ve_p$ are the standard basis vectors.

:::
